request: what is a unit vector

beats.intent: A vector three units long on the grid
beats.narration: Here is a vector v, pointing up and to the right, three units long.
beats.code:
stage.title("Unit vectors")
p = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2.4, 1.8), label="v")
stage.caption("v has length 3")

beats.intent: A copy of v shrinking to one third along the same line
beats.narration: Shrink a copy of v by a factor of three. It keeps its direction but is now exactly one unit long.
beats.code:
u = draw_vector(stage, p, (2.4, 1.8), color=GREEN)
scale_vector(stage, p, u, 1 / 3)
stage.label(u, r"\hat{u}", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)
stage.caption("Same direction, length 1")

beats.intent: The unit circle with i-hat, j-hat and u all touching it
beats.narration: Every unit vector ends on the circle of radius one: i-hat, j-hat and our new u.
beats.code:
r1 = np.linalg.norm(p.c2p(1, 0) - p.c2p(0, 0))
ring = Circle(radius=r1, color=TEAL).move_to(p.c2p(0, 0))
stage.play(Create(ring))
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)
stage.caption("Every unit vector ends on the unit circle")

beats.intent: Divide v by its length to get u
beats.narration: To make any vector a unit vector, divide it by its own length.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\hat{u} = \frac{v}{\|v\|}", r"= \frac{(2.4,\ 1.8)}{3}", r"\hat{u} = (0.8,\ 0.6)", where="right")
stage.pause(1.5)

request: why is the dot product negative when two vectors point away from each other

beats.intent: v's shadow landing along w when they point the same way
beats.narration: Take w along the x-axis and v up and to the right. Drop v's shadow onto w's line: it points the same way as w.
beats.code:
stage.title("Sign of the dot product")
p = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
w = draw_vector(stage, p, (3, 0), color=BLUE, label="w")
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 2), label="v")
drop = DashedLine(p.c2p(2, 2), p.c2p(2, 0), color=GREY_B)
s = Arrow(p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(2, 0), buff=0, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(drop), GrowArrow(s))
eq = stage.equation(r"v \cdot w = 2 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 0 = 6", where="right")
stage.caption("Shadow along w: positive")

beats.intent: v swung past ninety degrees, its shadow pointing backwards
beats.narration: Now swing v round so it leans away from w. Its shadow flips and points against w.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
p2 = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
w2 = draw_vector(stage, p2, (3, 0), color=BLUE, label="w")
v2 = draw_vector(stage, p2, (-2, 1.5), label="v")
drop2 = DashedLine(p2.c2p(-2, 1.5), p2.c2p(-2, 0), color=GREY_B)
s2 = Arrow(p2.c2p(0, 0), p2.c2p(-2, 0), buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(Create(drop2), GrowArrow(s2))
eq2 = stage.equation(r"v \cdot w = (-2)(3) + (1.5)(0)", r"v \cdot w = -6", where="right")
stage.caption("Shadow against w: negative")

beats.intent: The cosine formula beside the backwards shadow
beats.narration: The dot product is the lengths times the cosine of the angle, and the cosine turns negative past ninety degrees.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeOut(eq2))
stage.equation(r"v \cdot w = |v|\,|w|\cos\theta", r"\theta > 90^\circ \Rightarrow v \cdot w < 0", where="right")
stage.caption("Pointing apart means a negative dot product")

request: show me what stretching the plane horizontally does

beats.intent: The grid with i-hat, j-hat and a vector v
beats.narration: Start with the grid, the two basis vectors, and a vector v at one, one.

stage.title("A horizontal stretch")
p = draw_plane(stage)
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 1), color=YELLOW, label="v")

beats.intent: The grid pulled sideways to twice its width
beats.narration: Stretch everything along the x-axis by two. i-hat doubles, j-hat does not move, and v leans over.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[2, 0], [0, 1]], riders=[i_hat, j_hat, v])
stage.caption("x doubles, y stays the same")

beats.intent: The unit square becoming a two-by-one rectangle
beats.narration: Follow the unit square: it becomes a rectangle two wide and one tall, so every area doubles.

p2 = draw_plane(stage, where="left", x_extent=2)
sq, area = show_determinant(stage, p2, [[2, 0], [0, 1]])

stage.pause(1.5)

request: acceleration is how fast velocity changes - show it on a graph

beats.intent: A velocity curve rising faster and faster
beats.narration: Plot a car's velocity against time: it starts at one and climbs ever more steeply.
beats.code:
stage.title("Acceleration")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 5), y_range=(0, 12), labels=("t", "v"))
vel = lambda t: 0.4 * t ** 2 + 1
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, vel, color=BLUE, label="v(t)")

beats.intent: Staircase steps showing each second's gain in velocity
beats.narration: Mark how much velocity is gained in each second. The red rises get taller: the car is accelerating more.
beats.code:
steps = VGroup(*[VGroup(Line(ax.c2p(t, vel(t)), ax.c2p(t + 1, vel(t)), color=GREY_B),
                        Line(ax.c2p(t + 1, vel(t)), ax.c2p(t + 1, vel(t + 1)), color=RED, stroke_width=6))
                 for t in range(5)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(s) for s in steps], lag_ratio=0.4), run_time=2.5)
stage.caption("Each second the gain in speed grows")

beats.intent: A tangent sliding along the velocity curve, its slope read out
beats.narration: Shrink the steps to an instant and you get the slope of the velocity curve. That slope is the acceleration.
beats.code:
stage.clear(keep=[ax, g])
tan = slide_tangent(stage, ax, vel, 0.5, 4)
stage.caption("Slope of velocity = acceleration")

beats.intent: The derivative of velocity
beats.narration: Here the acceleration is the derivative: zero point eight times t, growing steadily.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}", r"= \frac{d}{dt}\left(0.4t^2 + 1\right)", r"a(t) = 0.8\,t", where="right")
stage.pause(1.5)

request: what does the average value of a function over an interval mean

request: animate newton's method finding the square root of 2

beats.intent: The parabola x squared minus two crossing zero
beats.narration: To find the square root of two, look for where x squared minus two crosses zero.
beats.code:
stage.title("Newton's method")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 3.5), y_range=(-3, 8))
f = lambda x: x ** 2 - 2
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, f, label="x^2 - 2")
stage.caption("Where does it cross zero?")

beats.intent: The tangent at three sliding down to hit the axis at 1.83
beats.narration: Guess three. Follow the tangent line there down to the axis: it lands at about 1.83.
beats.code:
x0 = 3.0
x1 = x0 - f(x0) / (2 * x0)
d0 = Dot(ax.c2p(x0, f(x0)), color=YELLOW)
t0 = Line(ax.c2p(x0, f(x0)), ax.c2p(x1, 0), color=YELLOW)
stage.play(FadeIn(d0), Create(t0))
up1 = DashedLine(ax.c2p(x1, 0), ax.c2p(x1, f(x1)), color=GREY_B)
stage.play(Create(up1))
stage.caption("First step: 3 to 1.83")

beats.intent: A second tangent from 1.83 landing at 1.46
beats.narration: Go up to the curve and repeat: the next tangent lands at about 1.46, much closer.
beats.code:
x2 = x1 - f(x1) / (2 * x1)
d1 = Dot(ax.c2p(x1, f(x1)), color=ORANGE)
t1 = Line(ax.c2p(x1, f(x1)), ax.c2p(x2, 0), color=ORANGE)
stage.play(FadeIn(d1), Create(t1))
up2 = DashedLine(ax.c2p(x2, 0), ax.c2p(x2, f(x2)), color=GREY_B)
stage.play(Create(up2))
stage.caption("Second step: 1.83 to 1.46")

beats.intent: Zoomed in near the root, the third tangent all but hitting it
beats.narration: Zoom in. From 1.46 the next tangent lands at 1.4142, already right on the root.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(1.3, 1.9), y_range=(-0.5, 1.5), where="left")
g2 = plot_graph(stage, ax2, f)
x3 = x2 - f(x2) / (2 * x2)
t2 = Line(ax2.c2p(x1, f(x1)), ax2.c2p(x2, 0), color=ORANGE)
t3 = Line(ax2.c2p(x2, f(x2)), ax2.c2p(x3, 0), color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(t2))
stage.play(Create(DashedLine(ax2.c2p(x2, 0), ax2.c2p(x2, f(x2)), color=GREY_B)))
stage.play(Create(t3))
root = Dot(ax2.c2p(x3, 0), color=GREEN)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(root))
stage.caption("Third guess: 1.4142, on the root")

beats.intent: The update rule and the guesses closing in
beats.narration: Each step is x minus f over f prime, and the guesses go 3, 1.83, 1.46, 1.4142.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}", r"3 \to 1.83 \to 1.46 \to 1.4142", where="right")
stage.caption("The correct digits roughly double each step")

request: visualize a damped oscillation that dies out over time
